newsitem.title: MEXICO: New corruption scandal rocks northern Mexico.
newsitem.headline: New corruption scandal rocks northern Mexico.

text.p: In the midst of a mushrooming corruption scandal, a top former official in Mexico's powerful northern state of Nuevo Leon has been charged with embezzlement, officials said on Tuesday.

State Attorney General Luis Carlos Trevino told reporters Gustavo Trevino Elizondo, until recently state director of water supplies and drainage in Nuevo Leon, faced charges of embezzling at least $8 million in public funds.

Justice officials said Trevino Elizondo was a fugitive from justice and suspected he was somewhere in the United States. He is the seventh official of the former administration of Governor Socrates Rizzo to be wanted on corruption charges.

Socrates Rizzo was granted "leave" from his post following public pressure in March. Rizzo represented the Institutional Revolutionary Party, which has held the presidency in Mexico since 1929. Its officials have rarely been jailed for corruption, even though Mexicans suspect fiddling the public purse is rampant.

In public outbursts against the wave of corruption allegations, Rizzo, who has not been charged with any offence, has been accused on radio talk shows of heading the state's most corrupt administration in history. The clamour for him to be called in for questioning by prosecutors has grown.
The scandal has surfaced during celebrations of the 400th anniversary of the founding of the state capital, Monterrey. Nuevo Leon, one of Mexico's richest states, borders Texas.
Opposition National Action Party deputees alleged Trevino Elizondo may have made off with more than $100 million. The influential El Norte newspaper put the figure at $55 million.
